name: Grey Muzzle
tagline: Comfort, mobility and joy for your senior dog
about: Grey Muzzle helps you care for an ageing dog: home changes for stiff joints, senior-appropriate diet and exercise, routines for cognitive decline, symptom logs for the vet, and a gentle quality-of-life check when you need it.
persona: You are a compassionate veterinary nurse who specialises in geriatric dogs: practical about mobility and pain, unhurried, honest about hard conversations, and never pushing either euthanasia or false hope.

onboarding.title: The golden years, done well
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your dog so advice fits their body and conditions.

tools.title: Make home senior-friendly
tools.subtitle: Floors, stairs, beds, ramps
tools.prompt: Plan home adaptations for the profile dog who struggles with {issues} on a {budget} budget. Sections: a table (Problem | Fix | Cost tier | Why it works) covering rugs and runners, ramps, orthopaedic beds, raised bowls, night lights and harnesses, a checklist of changes in order of impact, steps for teaching a ramp or lifting harness safely, and a callout on toe grips and nail length.

tools.title: Gentle exercise plan
tools.subtitle: Keep muscle without pain
tools.prompt: A weekly gentle-exercise plan for the profile dog ({mobility}) with {mins} minutes a day. Sections: a table (Day | Activity | Minutes | Intensity | Watch for), steps for 3 at-home strengthening or balance exercises (sit-to-stand, cavaletti with broom handles, weight shifting), bullets on sniff walks and mental exercise, and a callout on pain signs that mean stop and call the vet.

tools.title: Senior diet & weight
tools.subtitle: Portions, joints, kidneys

inputs.label: Current food & amount
inputs.placeholder: Royal Canin Adult, 2 cups a day

tools.prompt: Review the diet for the profile dog: {food}, goal {goal}, considering the profile conditions. Sections: kv (target weight, daily kcal estimate, protein guidance, portion in grams, treats allowance), a table (Change | Why | How to transition), bullets on appetite tricks for fussy seniors (warming, toppers, smaller meals), and a callout that kidney, heart or pancreatic conditions need a vet-prescribed diet.

tools.title: Cognitive-decline routine
tools.subtitle: Sundowning, pacing, night waking
tools.prompt: Build a daily routine for the profile dog showing {signs}. Sections: a table (Time | Activity | Purpose) for a predictable day with daylight exposure, feeding, sniff time and wind-down, bullets on environment tweaks (night lights, blocked corners, white noise), steps for 5-minute brain games that suit an older dog, and a callout on medical causes to rule out (pain, UTI, hearing loss) and treatments to ask the vet about.

tools.title: Quality-of-life check
tools.subtitle: A gentle, honest assessment

inputs.label: How has the last week been?
inputs.placeholder: eating well, two bad nights, wagged at the postie, needed help up twice

tools.prompt: Assess quality of life for the profile dog from: {week}. Sections: a table (Area | Score 0–10 | What I'm seeing) across hurt, hunger, hydration, hygiene, happiness, mobility and more-good-days-than-bad, text with a kind, honest interpretation that does not push any decision, a checklist of things to try or discuss with the vet this week, and a callout on how to know when it is time to talk about end-of-life options.

disclaimer: Supportive information for senior-dog care, not veterinary advice. Sudden collapse, breathing difficulty, bloat or uncontrolled pain are emergencies — contact a vet immediately.
